name: overhead-from-the-top
prompt: Vertical photograph taken from the very top of an enormous tower of stacked paper inside a dark empty warehouse at night, the lens pointing straight down the sheer white cliff of page edges, which plunges away in steep foreshortened perspective to a wet concrete floor far below. Filling the near foreground, the top sheet lies flat with the words "THE RULES" printed on it in heavy black capital letters, pin-sharp. At the foot of the tower, small and a little soft, five members of a modern British gang crane their heads straight up at the lens: today's hoodies, puffer jackets, work boots, black gloves on every hand, sleeves over the wrists, no skin anywhere. Each wears a knitted balaclava in a different dark colour (navy, bottle green, charcoal, oxblood, black) with no eye, nose or mouth openings, a thick white ring stitched around the whole face and a small red triangle inside the ring high on the right of the picture at two o'clock, never in the centre; plain cloth, no metal or lights. Their hand torches point upwards, the white beams cutting through floating dust and climbing the paper wall, and that torchlight makes the white rings and red triangles glint. A faint orange sodium glow leaks from a high warehouse window across one corner; everything else is deep black, broken only by hard pools of white light and puddle reflections on the floor. Wide-angle lens, deep vertical drop, high contrast, 35mm film grain, dizzying sense of looking down from a great height.
